items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I knew pretty early on that Lawrence wasn’t for me

ctx.x: I remember on the television, I remember distinctly, I remember two things, I remember Lawrence Welk was on the television and then there was a lot of country music on the television. I remember at the time there was these sort of country shows and there was like a young girl, I think a brother and sister that played like guitars and mandolins and they used to play double neck things, like mandolin on one and then six string on the other. And they were like, three feet high, I mean these were kids. And they were…

music that my parents listened to, we didn’t really have music in the house in terms of there was no, there was a victrola I guess, not a wind-up kind I mean you actually plugged it in and it went around, you didn’t have to crank it up, you know, I’m not quite that old. So they bought me a record player. I think the music came from outside the house. Because the only music in the house really was Lawrence and this country stuff. And I knew pretty early on that Lawrence wasn’t for me. I don’t know, something just…
What about the rock & roll of the day, the Ventures and all that kind of thing?
